researcher_notes: Sources swept: firm websites (team/contact pages, fetched with curl and parsed to text), SEC IAPD Form ADV Part 1 (api.adviserinfo.sec.gov firm search + reports.adviserinfo.sec.gov ADV PDFs parsed with pdftotext) for every RIA and for Post Oak Energy Capital, plus BusinessWire/PRNewswire/Newswire releases, Houston Business Journal, TechCrunch, Fortune, VCWire, WealthManagement.com, Rigzone, AltAssets and Mergr. No browser sessions were used. WHAT IS THIN: (1) Named person emails are rare in this segment - only 4 candidates publish one (Green Heron, Black Skimmer, Post Oak Private Wealth, and Artemis which was rejected). (2) Several PE/VC firms publish no street address and/or no phone (Green Heron, Milton Street, LDR, Saddle Ridge, South Loop, Soul Street, Modi, First Bight, ETV, Black Skimmer); those fields are null rather than guessed. (3) Employee counts for private funds are not authoritative - where given for PE/VC they are counts of named professionals on the firm's own team page or a LinkedIn company size band, and the source URL says which. RIA employee counts and AUM are exact Form ADV Item 5.A / 5.F figures. (4) Houston search funds are almost all single-principal vehicles; Prudentia Group was rejected as an explicit solopreneur, and Saddle Ridge and Black Skimmer are included but flagged as very small. (5) Four otherwise-strong Houston firms (Pelican Energy, TXE, Artemis, Rock Hill) were moved to rejected because their team pages already list a dedicated executive assistant or executive administrator. (6) Weakest triggers, flagged for the verifier: Valedor Partners (structural, undated), First Bight Ventures (self-stated Fund II, undated) and Mercury Fund (portfolio lead round rather than a firm-level event). (7) Two Houston firms surfaced via LinkedIn - Stoutbridge Capital and Del Monte Capital - had no reachable website and were rejected rather than sourced from aggregators alone.
